:::{#exr-fisher-kl-curvature}
#### Curvature of the Kullback--Leibler divergence

Let $\vX$ be a continuous random vector with density $\p(\vx \mid \param)$
for a scalar parameter $\param$, under the assumptions of @thm-score-mean-zero.
Let $\param_0$ be the true parameter value,
and define

$$
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\param)
\eqdef \Expp_{\param_0}\sb{\log \frac{\p(\vX \mid \param_0)}{\p(\vX \mid \param)}},
$$

the [Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence)
of the model with parameter $\param$ from the model with parameter $\param_0$.
Find $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\param_0)$, $D_{\mathrm{KL}}'(\param_0)$ and $D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\param_0)$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-fisher-kl-curvature}

Write $\llik(\param) = \log \p(\vX \mid \param)$.
All expectations below are taken under $\param_0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\param_0)
&= \E{\log \frac{\p(\vX \mid \param_0)}{\p(\vX \mid \param_0)}}
&& \text{(substitute $\param = \param_0$)}\\
&= \E{\log 1}
&& \text{(a nonzero number divided by itself is 1)}\\
&= \E{0}
&& \text{($\log 1 = 0$)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(the expectation of a constant is that constant)}
\end{aligned}
$$

For the derivatives, first separate the two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\param)
&= \E{\llik(\param_0) - \llik(\param)}
&& \text{(log of a ratio is a difference of logs)}\\
&= \E{\llik(\param_0)} - \E{\llik(\param)}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The first term does not depend on $\param$,
so its derivative is zero.
Exchanging differentiation and expectation, as in @thm-score-mean-zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}'(\param)
&= -\deriv{\param} \E{\llik(\param)}
&& \text{(the derivative of a constant is 0)}\\
&= -\E{\deriv{\param} \llik(\param)}
&& \text{(exchange derivative and expectation)}\\
&= -\E{\score(\param)}
&& \text{(definition of the score, evaluated at $\param$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

At $\param = \param_0$, @thm-score-mean-zero gives $\E{\score(\param_0)} = 0$,
so $D_{\mathrm{KL}}'(\param_0) = 0$.
Differentiating once more:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\param)
&= -\deriv{\param} \E{\score(\param)}
&& \text{(differentiate $D_{\mathrm{KL}}'$)}\\
&= -\E{\deriv{\param} \score(\param)}
&& \text{(exchange derivative and expectation)}\\
&= \E{-\hess(\param)}
&& \text{(the Hessian is the derivative of the score)}
\end{aligned}
$$

At $\param = \param_0$, this is the [expected information](#def-einf):
$D_{\mathrm{KL}}''(\param_0) = \einf(\param_0)$.

:::
